collections.title: Devotional
collections.intro: Krishna, Radha, Ganesha, Vitthal, the Buddha: faces I grew up seeing in prayer rooms and at festivals. I paint them the way I remember them, in deep blues and saffron, eyes closed or softly open, with the gold laid in one small dot at a time.

collections.title: Mandala Studies
collections.intro: Mandalas are where I slow down. Each one grows outward from a single point, ring by ring, dot by dot, with the tip of a brush and a lot of patience, until the whole surface hums.

collections.title: Portraits
collections.intro: Faces of people I love, and of people someone else loves. I paint the mood more than the likeness: the tilt of a head, the warmth of a cheek, the colour a moment felt like.

collections.title: Murals
collections.intro: A wall is the biggest canvas I get. I’ve painted one at home and one on site in Bhopal, and I’d love to paint yours: a home, an office, a café, a school or a studio, anywhere a blank wall could hold a story.

collections.title: Small Works
collections.intro: Little canvases, sketchbook spreads and paintings on wood, made in between the bigger pieces. Quick, personal and sometimes a joke: a sunflower, a very happy cat, a figure escaping through the Esc key.

works.title: Krishna and Radha
works.alt: Krishna in a striped saffron turban with a peacock feather, his cobalt-blue face beside Radha’s green-and-white face, against a mottled ochre ground
works.note: I started with Krishna’s blue face and let everything else find its place around it: the striped saffron turban, the peacock feather, Radha close beside him in green and white. I wanted it to hold the quiet closeness of two people who don’t need to look at each other to know the other is there. The ochre ground went on in thin, mottled layers so it feels warm and old, like a temple wall.

works.title: Om Mandala
works.alt: A dot-work mandala on deep ultramarine: a glowing saffron Om at the centre, ringed with yellow, white and blue dots and pale blue fan motifs
works.note: Dot work from the first mark to the last, built over many evenings, a few rings at a time. The Om sits at the centre because that’s where every mandala begins: one point, and everything else radiating out of it. Saffron on ultramarine felt like a lamp lit in the dark.

works.title: Child Portrait
works.alt: A sleeping child resting their chin in both hands, painted in rose, vermilion and magenta over a violet ground, with small sculpted roses at the edges
works.note: A little one asleep with their chin in their hands: the kind of moment that lasts a few seconds and stays with you for years. I painted it in rose, vermilion and magenta over violet, and added small sculpted roses at the edges. Personal pieces like this are close to my heart. If you have a moment like it, I’d love to paint it for you.

works.title: Ganesha
works.alt: A stylised Ganesha in soft cobalt and periwinkle blue, a raised saffron hand and great curves of orange and vermilion against black, with a red hibiscus in the corner
works.note: Ganesha is often the first figure I paint when I begin something new. Here I kept him in soft cobalt and periwinkle, let great curves of saffron and vermilion move around him, and set it all on black so the colour glows. The red hibiscus in the corner is his favourite flower.

works.title: Mandala Wall Mural
works.alt: A half-mandala painted on a pale wall, rising in layered petals of crimson, saffron, yellow, lilac and turquoise, with large teal leaves at its edges
works.note: This wall is at home. A half-mandala rising in layered petals of crimson, saffron, yellow, lilac and turquoise, with big teal leaves at its edges. It taught me how differently paint behaves on a wall than on canvas, and how much a room changes when one wall starts to bloom.

works.title: Think Out of the Box
works.alt: A chalkboard-black wall mural reading Think Out of the Box in pale blue, with a glowing lightbulb full of gears and a cascade of blue, yellow and white squares; the artist stands beside it pointing to the work
works.note: Painted on site in Bhopal. A chalkboard-black wall, the words in pale blue, a lightbulb full of gears and squares tumbling out of the box: a small nudge to think a little differently every time someone walks past it.

works.title: Vitthal
works.alt: Vitthal with closed eyes and a white tilak, a tall saffron-and-gold crown set with blue petal jewels, and sunburst earrings, on deep indigo
works.note: Vitthal is all stillness: eyes closed, a calm white tilak, waiting patiently for his devotees. I wanted the painting to feel just as patient, so all the movement went into the crown, saffron and gold set with blue petal jewels, and the deep indigo around him keeps everything else quiet.

works.title: Flute and Veena
works.alt: A serene face with a red forehead mark and gold-beaded hair, a small blue Krishna playing the flute behind her and a veena across the foreground, in cobalt and sky blue
works.note: Two instruments, two kinds of devotion: Krishna’s flute behind her and the veena resting across the front. I kept the whole painting in blues, from cobalt to sky, so the gold beads in her hair and the small red mark on her forehead would be its only warm notes.

works.title: Krishna and a Child
works.alt: Seen from behind, Krishna with a leaf in his hair and a child in a yellow dress lean on a railing together against a soft green ground
works.note: Krishna and a child leaning on a railing together, seen from behind. No faces, just company. I love the idea of the divine as a friend you can stand beside and look out at the world with.

works.title: The Escape Key Exists for a Reason
works.alt: A small figure climbs out of a dark keyboard, lifting the Esc key like a hatch, under the words The escape key exists for a reason
works.note: Painted at the end of a day spent staring at a screen. I build software by day and paint by evening, and this is where the two met: a little figure climbing out of the keyboard through the Esc key. The joke is for anyone who has ever needed a way out of a long day.

works.title: Just Bloom
works.alt: An open sketchbook painted saffron orange with white lotus line drawings and the words Just Bloom in red script, styled with foam roses
works.note: A sketchbook spread painted saffron, with white lotus line drawings and “Just Bloom” lettered in red. It’s a note to myself as much as anything: grow where you are, at your own pace.

works.title: Radha and Krishna in Blue
works.framing: Framed, black frame with white mount
works.alt: Radha with closed eyes, a red tilak and a crown of golden dots, a sweep of cream and gold behind her, and a small blue Krishna playing the flute in the corner, on a bright blue ground
works.note: Radha with her eyes closed and a crown of golden dots, lost in the music, and a small blue Krishna with his flute in the corner. To me it’s about devotion as a way of listening. This one was framed and shown at an exhibition, hung above my orange-and-blue Ganesha.

works.title: Buddha with Lotus
works.alt: Half of a serene green Buddha face with closed eyes and a long blue earlobe, a coral lotus below, on a dark green shimmering ground, signed Anushka 28/06/22
works.note: Half a face, eyes closed, a long blue earlobe and a coral lotus below. I wanted the stillness to feel as if the rest of the Buddha were just outside the frame. The dark green ground has a shimmer that shifts as you walk past it. Signed and dated 28/06/22.

works.title: Sunflower
works.alt: A close-up sunflower: long saffron and lemon petals around a dark seed head flecked with green, on deep navy
works.note: A sunflower painted close enough to count the seeds. I wanted the petals to look as if they were still opening, saffron and lemon reaching out against a deep navy night.

works.title: Blue Butterfly
works.alt: A large black butterfly with blue-and-white wing panels and dotted edges, resting by blue tulips on bands of green
works.note: A big black butterfly with blue-and-white wings, stopping for a moment beside blue tulips. From the year I mostly painted whatever made me happy that week.

works.title: Little Elephant
works.alt: A watercolour baby elephant in blue with a yellow ear, curled up with its trunk raised, blowing three red hearts, over a blue sky melting into orange and pink
works.note: A tiny watercolour elephant, curled up and blowing hearts into a sunset sky. Made to make someone smile, and it did.

works.title: Peacock
works.alt: A royal-blue peacock with a golden beak against a yellow ground and swirling green tail feathers with blue-and-orange eyes
works.note: A royal-blue peacock on a sunny yellow ground, its tail swirling round in green with blue-and-orange eyes. A small, bright piece, framed under glass and ready to hang.

works.title: Little Buddha
works.alt: A smiling little monk in blue robes sitting on a pink lotus, white rays around him on a sky-blue ground, signed Anushka
works.note: A smiling little monk sitting on a pink lotus, with white rays around him on sky blue. I painted this one outdoors, sitting on a rock, and I think some of that open air found its way in.

works.title: Happy Cat
works.alt: A grinning ginger cat with closed eyes, a red heart nose and long white whiskers, sitting tall against a speckled cobalt-blue ground, signed Anushka
works.note: A very pleased ginger cat with a red heart for a nose, painted on wood on a speckled cobalt ground. No deep meaning here: just the face every cat makes when the sun is warm.

works.title: Lightning
works.alt: A sketchbook page of branching yellow-white lightning over a smoky orange and red sky, with paint tubes and brushes beside it
works.note: A page from my watercolour sketchbook: branching lightning over a smoky orange and red sky. I wanted to catch the split second when the whole sky lights up.

works.title: Bicycle with Flowers
works.alt: A rust-orange bicycle with a basket of white and blue flowers against a deep blue wash, styled with foam roses and brushes
works.note: A rust-orange bicycle with a basket of white and blue flowers, against a deep blue wash. The kind of slow afternoon I’d like to be having: somewhere to go, and no hurry to get there.

works.title: Rising Mandala
works.alt: Half a mandala rising from the bottom edge, its petals and leaves washed in coral, green, teal and blue, outlined in black ink with white dots, against a black sky
works.note: Half a mandala, rising like the sun from the bottom edge. The petals and leaves are washed in soft coral, green and blue, then outlined in black and finished with white dots, ring by ring. The black sky at the top keeps the colours glowing.

works.title: Desert Cactus
works.alt: A green-and-blue patterned cactus standing on yellow and orange dunes under a huge orange sun and a magenta sky, every band filled with black line patterns
works.note: A cactus standing tall in the desert, under a sun that fills half the sky. Every band of sky, dune and cactus is filled with its own little pattern in black ink: scales, waves, zigzags and dots. The brightest colours I own, all on one small card.

works.title: Little Ganesha in Blue
works.alt: A simple pink-and-crimson Ganesha with a yellow crown, a raised blessing hand and a modak, seated against swirling sky-blue brushstrokes with white lines and dots
works.note: A small, simple Ganesha: a crimson trunk, pink ears, a yellow crown, one hand raised in blessing and a modak held close. The blue around him is painted in loose swirls so he feels light, with a few white lines and dots for rhythm.

works.title: Dragonfly
works.alt: A green dragonfly with pale pink wings flying across a tall, narrow strip that fades from red and orange into teal and yellow, with white bubbles floating around it
works.note: A dragonfly crossing a sky that melts from red and orange into teal and yellow. It is a tall, narrow piece, a little like a bookmark, with white bubbles drifting around the wings.

works.title: Devi with Lotus
works.alt: A serene goddess with closed eyes, gold jewellery and long dark hair, in a red sari, rising behind a large pink lotus against a red-and-gold glow and a deep blue night
works.note: A goddess with her eyes closed, gold at her ears and throat, her long hair falling around a red sari. She rises behind a big pink lotus, with a red-and-gold glow behind her and deep blue at the edges.

works.title: Shiva in Blue
works.alt: Shiva painted entirely in blues and violets: eyes closed, three ash lines and a third eye on his forehead, a crescent moon in his hair, a rudraksha mala and a serpent at his neck
works.note: Shiva in meditation, painted only in blues and violets. Eyes closed, the three lines and the third eye on his forehead, the crescent moon caught in his hair, a rudraksha mala and a serpent at his neck. I wanted the stillness to come from the colour as much as the face.

works.title: Ganesha in Colour
works.alt: An abstract Ganesha in bold blocks of colour: a blue trunk and yellow crown, dark green ears, a big yellow belly ringed with dots, against orange, red and a yellow side panel
works.note: Ganesha reduced to a few bold shapes: a blue trunk, a yellow crown, dark green ears and a round yellow belly ringed with dots. Orange and red behind him, and a yellow panel on the side. It comes framed in a dark wooden frame with glass.

works.title: Buddha in Green
works.alt: A grey Buddha head with closed eyes, the lower face hidden behind a green lotus and leaves, with white lotuses on either side, against streaks of green, ochre and teal
works.note: A grey stone-like Buddha, eyes closed, his face half hidden behind a green lotus and its leaves. White lotuses float on either side, and the background is pulled down in long streaks of green, ochre and teal, like light through water.
